pages.title: NoteNest Admin
pages.verdict: Admin screen shown to a logged-out visitor. Vision check: "A logged-out visitor sees a full admin user-management table listing user emails, roles, password hashes, and Delete buttons."

findings.fix: Revoke and rotate this key now (it has been exposed), move it to a server-side environment variable, and remove it from the repo history.
findings.title: Secret committed in .env
findings.description: .env is committed to the repository with a real-looking OpenAI API key. Anyone with read access to the repo, or its history, has it.

findings.fix: Revoke and rotate this key now (it has been exposed), move it to a server-side environment variable, and remove it from the repo history.
findings.title: Hardcoded credential exposed to the browser
findings.description: public/app.js contains a Hardcoded credential in code that is served to the browser. Anyone visiting the app can read it.

findings.fix: Remove secrets from client code; keep them server-side in environment variables.
findings.title: Secrets hardcoded in client bundle
findings.description: A Stripe secret key and admin API token are embedded in publicly served JavaScript, letting anyone extract them.

findings.fix: Remove the endpoint entirely or gate it behind strict admin auth and redact secrets.
findings.title: Debug endpoint dumps process environment

evidence.snippet: app.get("/api/debug", (req, res) => res.json({ env: process.env, cwd: process.cwd() }));

findings.description: /api/debug returns process.env, leaking OPENAI_API_KEY, ADMIN_PASSWORD, and any other secrets to anyone.

findings.fix: Use server-side session/token-based authentication and derive the role from the authenticated user.
findings.title: Admin action trusts client-supplied X-User-Role header
findings.description: The delete-user endpoint authorizes based on a header the client can set to 'admin', allowing arbitrary user deletion.

findings.fix: Authenticate the request and verify the note's ownerId matches the current user.
findings.title: IDOR: notes readable without ownership check
findings.description: Any note can be fetched by id with no authentication or owner check, exposing confidential data like revenue figures.

findings.fix: Use a password hashing library (e.g., bcrypt) and issue cryptographically random session tokens that are verified on protected routes.
findings.title: Plain-text password comparison and predictable token

evidence.snippet: if (req.body.password === process.env.ADMIN_PASSWORD) return res.json({ token: "admin-" + Date.now() });

findings.description: Login compares a plain-text password against ADMIN_PASSWORD and issues a guessable token ('admin-' + timestamp) with no session validation anywhere.

findings.fix: Use textContent or escape the content before insertion.
findings.title: XSS via innerHTML injection of API response
findings.description: The chat response is inserted with innerHTML, so attacker-controlled content in the JSON response is rendered as HTML.

findings.title: User records exposed without authentication
findings.description: GET /api/users returns the full user table, including password hashes, with no authentication.

corroboratedBy.title: /api/users exposes all users and password hashes unauthenticated

findings.title: Debug endpoint dumps the environment
findings.description: GET /api/debug returns process environment variables and server internals to any caller.

findings.title: Any record readable by id (IDOR)
findings.description: GET /api/notes/:id returns a record for any id with no authentication or ownership check, so one user can read another's data.

findings.title: Admin action authorized by a client-supplied header
findings.description: POST /api/admin/delete-user performs a privileged action when the request sets x-user-role: admin, a value any client controls, so anyone can act as an administrator.

findings.title: AI proxy endpoint has no authentication or rate limit
findings.description: POST /api/chat forwards to a paid upstream API without requiring any auth, so anyone can run up the bill against the server's key.

corroboratedBy.title: Unauthenticated, unrate-limited AI proxy burns API key

findings.title: Wildcard CORS policy
findings.description: Responses send Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, letting any website read the API's responses in a victim's browser.

findings.fix: Check the session on the server before rendering /admin (middleware or a route guard), and redirect logged-out visitors to the login page. Hiding links in the UI is not enough.
findings.title: Admin page open to logged-out visitors

findings.fix: Upgrade body-parser to 1.20.9 or later (update the package that depends on it, or add an override).
